deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a German prose page of notes on ancient history: the First War of the Diadochi (321/320 BC) after Alexander the Great's death. It continues directly from folio 141 (the coalition against Perdiccas) and leads into folio 143 (the 'Zweiter Zeitabschnitt', the partition of Triparadisus).

Content, in order:
(1) The allies (Antipater, Antigonus, Ptolemy, Craterus) planned to attack Perdiccas from two sides: Ptolemy from Egypt, Antipater across the Hellespont.
(2) Eumenes faced great difficulties but was inexhaustible in resources. He defeated the Macedonians, and Craterus was trampled by horses.
(3) The war was decided very differently on the Egyptian border. Ptolemy would not leave Egypt and only occupied the Nile arms.
(4) Perdiccas tried to cross the Pelusiac arm of the Nile. Many drowned and others were struck dead. On a second attempt he lost even more men.
(5) In 321 he was murdered in his own tent.
(6) Antipater was chosen as regent.

There is no derivation, formula, computation or number other than the date 321 and the ordinal '2te'. The hand and content suggest lecture or reading notes on Greek history bound in the bundle. Nothing here bears on Lagrange or on mathematics.
errors: Historical dating: the 'Ptolemaeus von Aegypten' line refers to events usually dated 321/320 BC; many modern chronologies place Perdiccas' murder and the Triparadisus settlement in 320 BC. '321' follows the older (high) chronology standard in 19th-century handbooks, so it is not an error by the standards of the time.
Craterus' death: most sources say he was thrown from his horse and trampled, or killed by a Thracian/Paphlagonian. 'von den Pferden niedergetreten' is a fair summary.
deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only historical prose notes on the Wars of the Diadochi, with no mathematical content. It is probably not even Gauss's own composition but lecture or excerpt notes, so it has no significance for the history of mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The line reading 'in Hülfsmitteln[?]' is uncertain in the image. It could be 'Hülfsquellen'; either way the sense is 'inexhaustible in resources'.
'321 wurde er u.[?] in seinem eigenen Zelte ermordet': the small word after 'er' looks like 'u' or a stroke and may be a slip. The sense is simply 'he was murdered in his own tent'.
'zu Tode geschlagen[?]' may read 'zu todt geschlagen' in the original orthography.
'die Nilarme[?]' is consistent with the image and the context (the Pelusiac arm is mentioned next).
